title: Alpha Illusion — LLM Trading Agent Validation Checklist (arXiv:2605.16895)
description: Create wiki page at wiki/trading/algorithms/llm-alpha-validation.md documenting the 6 structural validity tests from 'The Alpha Illusion' (Sheng et al., 2025, arXiv:2605.16895) that must be passed before LLM trading agent alpha claims are deployment evidence. Integrate with existing multi-agent-llm-trading.md and llm-trading-agent-benchmarks-2026.md. The six tests: (1) Temporal integrity — no look-ahead bias; training uses only data available at signal generation time; (2) Real-world frictions — commissions, spread, market impact, short borrow costs; (3) Counterfactual robustness — does the strategy outperform simple baselines (buy-and-hold, random, equal-weight)? (4) Predictive calibration — are stated confidence levels accurate? High-confidence trades should outperform low-confidence ones; (5) Numerical execution — can the strategy actually be executed? Position sizes that exceed daily volume, untradeable instruments, or unrealistic fill prices must be modeled; (6) Multi-agent disaggregation — in ensemble systems, does removing any single agent significantly degrade performance? (Tests for genuine complementarity vs redundancy). Cross-reference: systems audited include FinCon, FinMem, TradingAgents, FinAgent, QuantAgent, FLAG-Trader. Apply these 6 tests to H274 (multi-agent PEAD), H381 (AlphaLogics), H382 (FactorEngine), H383 (HMM+RL), and any future LLM-based proposals as a validation gate before production consideration. Add checklist to wiki/trading/shared-eval-checklist.md.
rationale: The Alpha Illusion paper documents that LLM trading agent Sharpe ratios reported in literature (often >2.0) routinely fail one or more of these 6 tests when examined carefully. This is directly relevant to our pipeline: H381/H382/H384 all use LLM-generated factors; H274 uses multi-agent debate. Without systematic application of these tests, we risk promoting LLM-generated strategies to paper trading that have inflated IS performance. This wiki page codifies the checklist as a permanent reference for the hypothesis evaluation workflow. Maps directly onto our existing shared-eval-checklist.md 7-point gate — adds LLM-specific sub-tests.
